_about: Every factual claim in Episode 003, with the narration segments that use it. Sources: fact_check.csv / sources.md. Calculations: calculations.py.

claims.claim: Hypothetical bundle: music $11.99, streaming $15.49, cloud storage $2.99, fitness $12.99, productivity $9.99, AI assistant $20.00 per month = $73.45/month, $881.40/year, $2.41/day.
claims.evidence: Hidden Ledger assumptions; calculations.json bundle_*.
claims.method_or_caveat: Labelled HYPOTHETICAL on screen and in narration ('a made-up example'). Prices are not those of any named service.

claims.claim: Two hypothetical companies: $120 one-time vs $10/month, 1,000 customers: $120,000 vs $10,000 in month one; $120,000 after 12 months if nobody cancels.
claims.evidence: calculations.json company_*.

claims.claim: Hypothetical unit economics: $10/month, developer keeps $7 (70%); expected lifetime ≈ 1/monthly churn: 10% churn → ~10 months → ~$70; 20% → ~5 months → ~$35; CAC $40.
claims.evidence: calculations.json ltv_*; 70% from Apple's first-year terms.
claims.method_or_caveat: 1/churn is the standard approximation of expected lifetime under constant churn; gross revenue to developer, before other costs.

claims.claim: RevenueCat State of Subscription Apps 2026 analyzed over 115,000 apps covering more than $16 billion in revenue; only apps integrated with RevenueCat.
claims.evidence: "we analyzed over 115,000 apps across all app categories, covering more than $16 billion in revenue across more than a billion transactions"; inclusion requires a RevenueCat integration.
claims.method_or_caveat: Population limitation stated in narration and on screen.

claims.claim: New subscription app launches: ~2,000 per month in Jan 2022; 14,700+ by Jan 2026.
claims.evidence: "~2,000 new subscription apps launched per month in Jan 2022; 14,700+ by Jan 2026."
claims.method_or_caveat: Launch data sourced by RevenueCat from Appfigures (report methodology).

claims.claim: Median monthly revenue one year after launch ~$72; top 10% above $2,574 (report: 'top 10% pull $2,500+').
claims.evidence: "Cross-category median is ~$72, but the top 10% pull $2,500+"; "If you’re above $2,574, you’re in the top 10%".

claims.claim: Only 4.6% of newly launched apps reach $10K monthly revenue within two years.
claims.evidence: "Only 4.6% of newly launched apps reach $10K in monthly revenue within two years."

claims.claim: Apps launched before 2020 generate 69% of all subscription revenue (in the data).
claims.evidence: "apps launched before 2020 generate 69% of all subscription revenue."

claims.claim: Median share of subscriptions still active after one year (2024 cohort): monthly 8%, yearly 28% (2023 cohort: 10%, 31%); subscription-level, not user-level metric.
claims.evidence: "Yearly: 31% → 28% median (-3%). Monthly: 10% → 8% median (-2%)." Key takeaway: "from the 2023 cohort to the 2024 cohort"; retention "is a subscription-level metric, not a user-level metric."
claims.method_or_caveat: Narration distinguishes subscriptions from people and payments from use.

claims.claim: Nearly half of monthly subscribers do not renew once.
claims.evidence: "Nearly half of monthly subscribers ... do not renew once." (1st monthly renewal medians 53–61% by category)

claims.claim: Hard paywalls convert ~5x freemium: 10.7% vs 2.1% download-to-paid by day 35; nearly identical year-one retention.
claims.evidence: "Hard paywalls convert five times better than freemium (10.7% vs 2.1% download-to-paid by day 35) with nearly identical year-one retention"

claims.claim: 23.2% of apps combine subscriptions with lifetime purchases ('nearly a quarter'); 63.5% are subscriptions-only.
claims.evidence: "Overall: 63.5% subs-only, 23.2% + lifetime, 10.7% + consumables, 2.5% all three."

claims.claim: Involuntary billing failures ≈31% of subscription cancellations on Google Play vs 14% on the App Store.
claims.evidence: "Nearly a third of all subscription cancellations on Google Play are involuntary billing failures — more than double the rate on the App Store (14%)." Headline figure 31%.

claims.claim: AI-powered apps generate 41% more revenue per payer but churn ~30% faster.
claims.evidence: "AI-powered apps generate 41% more revenue per payer, but they churn 30% faster."

claims.claim: Oracle: substantially all customers purchase and renew software support contracts annually.
claims.evidence: "Substantially all of our customers elect to purchase and renew their software support contracts annually."
claims.method_or_caveat: Used to show that recurring payments for software predate app subscriptions (business software).

claims.claim: May 2013: Adobe announced new creative innovations/features exclusively for Creative Cloud subscribers; CS6 the last major update for perpetual licensees.
claims.evidence: "In May 2013 we announced we would exclusively deliver new creative product innovations and features to Creative Cloud subscribers, and that Adobe Creative Suite 6 (“CS6”) ... would be the last major update we provide for perpetual licensees."

claims.claim: Adobe subscription revenue as % of total: FY2012 15%, FY2013 28%, FY2014 50%.
claims.evidence: Revenue table: "Subscription 2,076.6 1,137.9 673.2 ... Percentage of total revenue 50 % 28 % 15 %" (FY2014, FY2013, FY2012).

claims.claim: Adobe total revenue FY2012 $4,403.7M → FY2013 $4,055.2M (−8%).
Adobe net income FY2012 $832.8M → FY2013 $290.0M.
claims.method_or_caveat: Narrated $833M → $290M. Not attributed solely to the subscription switch.

claims.claim: Adobe FY2014: subscriptions 50% of revenue.
claims.evidence: See A02.

claims.claim: Adobe FY2025: total revenue $23,769M; subscription $22,904M = 96% of total.
claims.evidence: "Subscription $ 22,904 ... Percentage of total revenue 96 %"; "Total revenue $ 23,769".
claims.method_or_caveat: Narration adds that not all growth came from the switch.

claims.claim: Adobe still licenses perpetual versions of certain products.
claims.evidence: "We also license perpetual versions of certain products with maintenance and support"

claims.claim: Apple auto-renewable subscriptions: developer receives 70% in a subscriber's first year, 85% after one year of paid service (minus taxes).
claims.evidence: "During a subscriber's first year of service, you receive 70% of the subscription price ... After a subscriber accumulates one year of paid service, your net revenue increases to 85%"

claims.claim: App Store Small Business Program members receive 85% regardless of tenure.
claims.evidence: "If you're currently enrolled in the App Store Small Business Program, you receive 85% of the subscription price at each billing cycle ... regardless of whether or not the subscription has accumulated one year of paid service."

claims.claim: Sept 25, 2025: FTC announced a $2.5B settlement with Amazon ($1B civil penalty, $1.5B refunds) over alleged Prime enrollment without consent and difficult cancellation.
claims.evidence: FTC press release "FTC Secures Historic $2.5 Billion Settlement Against Amazon" (Sept 25, 2025): alleged Amazon "enrolled millions of consumers in Prime subscriptions without their consent" and used "a complex and difficult process" for cancellation.

claims.claim: Spotify: 290 million Premium Subscribers at Dec 31, 2025; 2025 revenue €17,186M.
claims.evidence: "Premium Subscribers were 290 million as of December 31, 2025"; "Revenue 17,186" (€ millions).
claims.method_or_caveat: Streaming service, explicitly distinguished from typical apps.

claims.claim: Spotify cost of revenue consists predominantly of royalty and distribution costs; €11,690M of €17,186M (68%); consolidated gross margin 32% in 2025.
claims.evidence: "Cost of revenue consists predominantly of royalty and distribution costs related to content streaming"; "Gross margin ... Consolidated 32 % 30 % 26 %".

claims.claim: Spotify operating loss €446M in 2023.
claims.evidence: "Operating income/(loss) 2,198 1,365 ( 446 )"

claims.claim: Spotify operating income €2,198M in 2025.
claims.evidence: See S03.
